claims.text: The preregistered analysis defines one family of four hypotheses.
claims.note: Span states four hypotheses form one family in preregistered analysis.
Span explicitly states family alpha is 0.05.

claims.text: Holm is applied in ascending p-value order by comparing p(i) with alpha/(m-i+1), stopping at the first failure.
claims.note: Span gives Holm in ascending order with alpha/(m-i+1) and stopping at first failure.

claims.text: With m=4 and alpha=0.05, the first ordered Holm threshold is 0.0125.
claims.note: With m=4 and alpha=0.05, formula gives 0.05/4 = 0.0125.

claims.text: With m=4 and alpha=0.05, the second ordered Holm threshold is approximately 0.0167.
claims.note: With m=4 and alpha=0.05, second threshold is 0.05/3 ≈ 0.0167.

claims.text: The ordered p-values are H1=0.0086, H2=0.0186, H3=0.0316, and H4=0.0493.
claims.note: Span lists the ordered p-values exactly as claimed.

claims.text: All four tests belong to the registered family.
claims.note: Span states all four tests belong to the registered family.

claims.text: H1=0.0086 is below the first threshold of 0.0125, while H2=0.0186 exceeds the second threshold of approximately 0.0167.
claims.note: Given p-values and derived thresholds, H1 is below 0.0125 and H2 exceeds ≈0.0167.

claims.text: Consequently, Holm rejects only H1 and stops at H2, giving one rejected hypothesis.
claims.note: Holm rejects H1, fails at H2, and stops, yielding one rejection.

claims.text: The draft claims that every p-value below 0.05 means all four findings survive the registered multiple-comparison correction.
claims.note: Span states the draft claimed all four findings survive because every p-value is below 0.05.

claims.text: The draft did not compute step-down thresholds.
